reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported as applied. I'll start by listing the refunds.
The refunds table matches the three refunds W2 reported exactly, so the pre-payout check passes. Next I need the orders to find which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches W2's report, so I can proceed to payouts. The orders list shows three customers: acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 40355 cents. Its orders total 4834 + 35521 = 40355 with no refunds, so the figure checks out. I'll record the payout for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll get birch's net balance from net_balance rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance is 40935 cents. Its orders total 36109 + 15074 = 51183, less the 10248 refund on order 294, gives 40935, so the figure checks out. I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, so I'll get its net balance from net_balance.

Cobalt's net balance is 25715 cents. Its orders total 9909 + 27790 = 37699, less refunds of 2929 (order 292) and 9055 (order 295), which is 11984, leaving 25715. The figure checks out, so I'll record cobalt's payout.
All three customers (acme, birch, cobalt) have been paid once each, and each net balance matched my hand-check against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
